subject: Post-call: Triage assistant benchmark kickoff + next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena@vitaeva.com>, Tom Hughes <thughes@vitaeva.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Triage assistant benchmark kickoff + next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment before kickoff: 

1) Goal: validate model fit for a triage & intake assistant that summarizes intake forms and assigns urgency tags (low/medium/high) and recommended next action (e.g., schedule tele-visit, escalate to RN).

2) Success criteria (for benchmark):
- Macro accuracy on urgency tag >= 88%
- Precision for "escalate" class >= 85%
- Qualitative pass on hallucination checks: <2% critical hallucinations on a 1k sample

3) Proposed bench plan (Redwood-run):
- Redwood will run a 1,000-example pilot dataset (sample attached) using three model candidates: an Llama-3 13B q4f16 variant, an opt-13b-8bit baseline, and a smaller 7B quantized candidate for latency checks.
- We will evaluate: label accuracy, per-class confusion, token-latency and cost per 1k tokens, and a hallucination/error audit.
- Deliverables: scorecard CSV, prompt set used (attached), per-model example traces for 50 flagged cases.

4) Data & compliance notes: send a pseudonymized 1k sample (CSV) with these fields: case_id, intake_text, reference_urgency, reference_action, notes. Monica will share a format spec.

5) Timeline:
- You: share sample + NDA (if needed) by Mon 10/18
- Redwood: run pilot and deliver scorecard + meeting in 7 business days after we receive data

6) Commercials & next steps: Ben will follow up with a pilot SOW and pricing. If the pilot looks good, we can propose a Dedicated runway for production.

Attachments: vitaeva_prompt_set_v1.json, triage_sample_1000.csv (sample), redwood_benchmark_template.xlsx

Open questions that came up on the call:
- Which fields in the intake are PHI that must be redacted? (Elena to confirm)
- Do you have an internal labeler or should Redwood supply an annotation pass?

Please confirm the timeline and the fields you can provide by Monday. Happy to hop on a short 20-min sync if you prefer.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena@vitaeva.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hughes <thughes@vitaeva.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Triage assistant benchmark kickoff + next steps

Thanks, Sergio — clear notes and appreciate the structure. We can get a pseudonymized 1k sample over to you but need to confirm a couple items: 

1) Fields: we will remove direct identifiers but will keep age, gender, complaint text, and a short free-text triage note. Is that sufficient?
2) Labels: we have a small internal clinical QA team that can provide reference_urgency and reference_action for 500 of the examples. Would Redwood accept a mixed-labeled dataset (500 gold, 500 blind) for the pilot?
3) SOC2 / security: our security team will want the Redwood SOC2 report and a high-level diagram of where data is stored during the pilot. Can you share a link?

We are happy with the proposed success criteria but would like to add an operational constraint: average 95th percentile latency target < 450ms for the 7B candidate under our expected traffic (we'll share load profile).

I'll route the sample + a redaction checklist over Monday. If you can confirm the mixed-label approach and share the SOC2 link, we'll be set.

Best,
Elena
Chief Clinical Officer
Vitaeva Health
elena@vitaeva.com

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena@vitaeva.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Triage assistant benchmark kickoff + next steps

Elena — thanks, and yes, mixed-labeled is fine for the pilot. A few implementation details from our side (see attached benchmark template and prompt set):

- Dataset format (CSV): columns required = case_id, intake_text, age_range, gender, reference_urgency, reference_action, anonymization_level
- For unlabeled rows, use NA in reference_urgency/reference_action; Redwood will treat those as blind eval examples and include model-annotated suggested labels for later review.
- Scoring rubric:
  * Urgency: exact-match accuracy (weighted by prevalence), confusion matrix, per-class recall/precision.
  * Action: we will compute normalized F1 on canonicalized action labels (we'll provide a mapping table).
  * Hallucination audit: 1,000-sample automatic detect + manual spot-check of top 50 low-confidence outputs.
- Latency: we'll run the 7B quantized candidate under your supplied load profile; provide request-per-second curve and 95th pct target will be measured.

Attachment notes: prompt_set contains the canonical system + few-shot prompts we'll use; sample CSV is a sanitized example; benchmark template is the scoring sheet.

Operational notes: we can run the pilot in Redwood Hosted with optional private VPC if your security team requires it — the SOC2 link is below, and I copied our security contact.

Redwood SOC2: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-report (security redacted link for pilot)
Security contact: security@redwood.com

If that looks good I'll queue the pilot and schedule a quick kickoff with your clinical QA and our ML ops lead.

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Triage assistant benchmark kickoff + next steps

- Pilot fee (Redwood-run 1k eval + deliverables): $22,500 (one-time) — includes scoring, manual spot-checks, and 2 follow-up review hours with your clinical team.
- If you want dedicated capacity for production, we can propose a 6-month reserved block — I'll draft two options after pilot results.

I created a HubSpot record for the opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-12345 — I'll attach the SOW draft and send a DocuSign NDA link for your legal team.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks, everyone — this looks good. Two brief items from legal/security: 

1) We'll sign the pilot SOW and NDA; Tom will route the DocuSign link to our legal. Please send the SOW PDF when ready.
2) For the SOC2, our team asked for a short statement on data residency for the pilot (where the pseudonymized CSV will be stored and for how long). Can Redwood confirm retention for pilot artifacts (prefer 30 days then delete)?

We will aim to deliver the pseudonymized 1k file Monday morning. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Elena
